caption: The drawing depicts a square piece of woven textile, shown centered on a plain, cream-colored background. The textile has a multicolored pattern, consisting primarily of red, blue, olive green, and white. The design features alternating horizontal stripes, each filled with intricate floral and geometric motifs. There are prominent sections of leafy and star-like shapes, along with stylized flower forms in the patterns. A vertical, irregular cream-colored wavy line runs from top to bottom, intersecting with the horizontal stripes. On the lower left portion, some text is integrated into the pattern: "WIN-MILVE KNOXING COUNTY OHIO JULY 21 OF A.D. MICHAEL IRUNE 1854 9," with the text mostly in white on a red or blue background. Fringes are visible along the bottom edge, and some threads are loose on the left side. The right and top edges are more neatly finished. The textile is rendered with careful detail, showing texture, weave, and the interplay of colors. In the bottom right corner of the blank background, the name "Eva Wilson" is written in small, reddish letters.
title: Jacquard Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
